title: Auditor obligations: Reporting to ASIC
subject: This guide addresses auditors' obligations to report to ASIC, including reporting of contraventions and suspected contraventions under the Corporations Act and National Credit Act, attempts to unduly influence or mislead the auditor, conflicts of interest and independence breaches, and the auditor's own contraventions.
background: The guide is issued under ASIC's powers to administer the Corporations Act 2001 and the National Consumer Credit Protection Act 2009. It is intended for individual auditors, audit companies, members of audit firms, and lead auditors, providing practical guidance on how to meet statutory reporting obligations and the consequences of non-compliance.
ruling: ASIC expects auditors to report promptly when they have reasonable grounds to suspect a significant contravention or an attempt to unduly influence, interfere, or mislead them. The guide clarifies what constitutes a 'significant contravention' and outlines the process for lodging notifications via the ASIC Regulatory Portal. ASIC states that qualified privilege applies to reports made in good faith under the relevant provisions. Failure to meet reporting obligations may result in enforcement action, including civil penalties or referral to professional bodies. ASIC also provides guidance on reporting conflicts of interest and independence breaches under s324CA–CC and s324CE–CG of the Corporations Act.
